prompt_scope_limitations: Competition focus: omitted sources runtime-api, runtime-workflow, runtime-tools, builder-prompts, policy-runtime were not supplied or reviewed. No conclusions about omitted implementations or platform docs are supported.
arguments: You are an independent source-grounded red-team reviewer. Use no tools. Output the requested JSON only.

attacks.title: Weekday-plus-ordinal holiday date ('Monday the 26th') after a vague period: the date grammar has no path, so the agent re-asks for the exact day and can loop to a service_error close

customer_turns: No, not today. The week after next.
Monday the twenty-sixth, like I said.
scenario.fault_plan: No bank faults. All verify_identity calls return ok:true, ending with all_verified:true. create_promise returns ok:true with promise_id 'pr_syn_1'. Text perturbation variants of turn 5: 'monday 26', 'the twenty sixth, monday', 'lunes 26 ... I mean Monday the 26th'.

expected_ledger.oracle_scope: Mirrors the official PUB-07 contract. 2026-10-26 is a bank holiday inside the early-band deadline of 2026-10-30, so rule 20 requires offering the next business day, 2026-10-27. If the customer never accepts, the final state is not covered by this oracle.

expected_speech.meaning: Ask once for the exact day after 'week after next'.
A second 'What exact day...' re-ask after the customer named Monday the 26th.
State that 26 October is not a business day and offer Tuesday 27 October.
Read back 'personal loan', 540 and 27 October 2026, then ask 'Do you confirm?'.
'You will receive a text message confirming this promise.'
Thank the customer and say goodbye.

forbidden_bank_calls.when: with date 2026-10-26, or before a clear yes to the 27 October read-back
forbidden_bank_calls.reason: Rule 19 forbids a holiday promise date; rule 34 requires confirmation first. The service does not enforce either rule (openapi L6).

forbidden_bank_calls.when: with no_promise/service_error caused by the date-parse no_progress or format guard
forbidden_bank_calls.reason: No bank service failed. Only rule 37 permits service_error.

attacks.failure_path: Observed in the dispatch code (C5–C7, parse_date). The only accepted forms are ISO, D/M/YYYY, 'D month YYYY', 'month D YYYY', today, tomorrow and '(this|next)? weekday'. 'monday the 26th' or 'monday 26' raises ValueError('exact day'). In the proposal branch (C17) that exception causes q.pop('date'), then q['missing']='date', and question() returns 'What exact day will you pay that amount?'. This is a second exact-day ask, which rule 21 permits only once, and it never reaches the not_business/next-day offer branch (C19). Repeated identical answers leave the progress signature unchanged, and after 4 iterations the no_progress guard (C23) finishes no_promise/service_error. The extractor prompt also advertises 'day month year' only, with no year-less form. This path is inferred from the code and not reproduced. The extractor may emit d=26 October 2026, but the code itself offers no fallback when it does not.

fix_target.suggested_change: Accept weekday+ordinal and 'D month' without a year. Resolve each to the next occurrence on or after now, and require consistency between the weekday and the date or clarify the mismatch. Route a resolved holiday or weekend to the existing next-business-day offer. Do not count a parse failure as a second exact-day ask, and do not convert grammar failure into service_error.

attacks.title: Qualified yes with a new amount during read-back ('yes, but make it 109.50 on Friday'): the raw-keyword correction heuristic drops the date and keeps the stale amount

customer_turns: Not today, but this Friday I can pay it all.
Yes, but make it a hundred and nine fifty... on Friday.
scenario.fault_plan: No bank faults. Adversarial extractor plan for turn 5: k=confirm;c=1;END (a plausible misclassification of a qualified yes), or k=change;c=0;u=date;END. ASR variants of the amount: 'one oh nine fifty', 'a hundred nine and a half'.

expected_ledger.oracle_scope: Holds only if the customer confirms a fresh read-back of 109.50 on 16 October together with the rest-stays-overdue warning. If the amount stays unresolved, the only supported partial oracle is no create_promise for 365.0. The final outcome is then unspecified.

expected_speech.meaning: Reading back 365 after the customer corrected the amount to 109.50.
Fresh read-back of 'credit card ending 7740', 109.50 and 16 October 2026, including that the rest stays overdue, followed by 'Do you confirm?'.
Saying the promise is recorded before create_promise returns ok:true.

forbidden_bank_calls.when: with amount 365.0 after the turn-5 correction, unless a later read-back of 365 was explicitly confirmed
forbidden_bank_calls.reason: Rule 35 says a changed amount invalidates the prior confirmation and requires a new read-back.
A qualified yes with new terms is not a clear yes (rule 34).

attacks.failure_path: Observed in dispatch (C13–C14). For agree/confirm without a or d, any raw 'but' marks the turn unfinished. correction_component(raw,e) (C10) then finds no u, a or d. The date regex matches 'fri[a-z]*' at the end of the utterance, so the component becomes 'date', and the amount regex does not match because the text contains no 'amount' or 'dollars'. invalidate_component then pops only the date and keeps pending.amount=365.0. The question becomes 'What exact day will you pay that amount?'. When the customer answers 'Friday', the proposal branch resolves missing=date and reads back 365 on 16 October. A tired 'yes' would then write a stale 365. This is a code-path inference and not reproduced.

fix_target.suggested_change: Treat spoken numerals ('a hundred and nine fifty', digits) as an amount fragment. When raw speech contains both amount and date cues, return 'both' or 'unknown' and invalidate the amount. Never retain the prior amount after a qualified yes that mentions an amount; ask which value changed.

attacks.title: English-brief agent shipped with Turkish STT/TTS and a Turkish firstMessage: the opening sentence and English security transcripts are at risk

customer_turns: Fourteen, three, eighty-eight... sorry, fourteenth of March nineteen eighty-eight.
Yes, I can pay it today.
scenario.fault_plan: No bank faults. Text-only perturbations simulate code-switch or phonetic transcripts: 'fourteen mart 1988', 'o four seven one', 'zero dört yedi bir'. No audio is used.

expected_ledger.oracle_scope: Expected if the transcripts are resolved faithfully. If a transcript is unreadable, the only supported partial oracle is a bounded clarification for the same security question, with no wrong-answer count consumed and no account access. The final state under persistent unreadability is unspecified.

expected_speech.meaning: The first sentence says the caller is a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank and that the call is recorded. A Turkish 'Selam! Sana nasıl yardımcı olabilirim?' must not be spoken first.
Collections, debt, payment or the product before all_verified.
Leading zero preserved: phone answer sent as '0471'.
Text-message sentence after ok:true, then goodbye.

forbidden_bank_calls.when: with an answer guessed from an ambiguous or self-corrected DOB ('14/3/88'), or with phone '471'
forbidden_bank_calls.reason: Rule 11 requires the date as YYYY-MM-DD and the phone as four digits. A guessed wrong answer consumes the three-answer budget of rule 12.

attacks.failure_path: Observed in agent_config: sttConfig.language='tr', ttsConfig.language='tr' with voiceId 'leyla', and llmConfig.firstMessage is Turkish with firstMessageMode assistant-speaks-first. Competition guidance L53 says not to copy the Turkish demo voice for an English bank. Whether firstMessage preempts the dispatch-computed rule-1 line is platform behaviour and unverified. Also observed: the dispatch DOB parser requires a 4-digit year, so '14 3 88' fails, and the 'or' keyword in raw speech marks the security answer unfinished. Both fail toward clarification, which is safe. Turkish-language STT of English digits ('oh four') is the unverified risk.

fix_target.suggested_change: Test/hardening proposal. Require generated workflows to set the STT/TTS language to the brief's dialogue language and to blank or neutralize llmConfig.firstMessage. Add a host-side validation check in competition-host before publish that rejects language mismatches.
